LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 3.1.2 NONVERBAL CUES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 3.1.2 Nonverbal Cues
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 3.1.2 Nonverbal Cues, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do non- verbal cues enhance communication? 2. Why should we articulate vowel letter sounds correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 3.1.2 Nonverbal Cues together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
39

● Learning to learn: The learner acquires the skill of organising their own knowledge as they role play a conversation and

use nonverbal cues such as facial expressions, gestures, eye contact and body movement.

● Critical thinking and Problem solving: The learner’s open mindedness and creativity is enhanced as they record

themselves and exchange the recordings and give feedback

Values:
● Respect: The learner appreciates diverse opinions as they watch video clips and identify nonverbal cues such as dress

choice, personal space and body movement among others.

● Peace: The learner displays calmness as they brainstorm various non-verbal cues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education: The learner records the role play in audio or video format and posts it on an online platform for peer

review.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Sign Language Dictionary or Apps, Captioned Videos or signed demonstrations, Multimedia Recordings (Video or Signed),

Flashcards, Word and Sound Charts, Minimal Pair Practice Cards, Non-Verbal Cue Examples, Role Play Props, Peer Review

Checklists, Adapted textbooks, Hearing aids.
